Hi Ben —

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Opsly is lining up a short pilot (4–6 weeks) to move our conversational assistant from a best-effort cloud-hosted endpoint to a dedicated GPU carveout. Before we book a workshop, can you send your pre-sales sizing questions so we can give you realistic telemetry?

Quick context:
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~30 RPS API calls, with a 3x burst window during peak marketing hours (~90 RPS for ~20 minutes).
- Prompt/response: typical prompt ~70–100 tokens, model responses ~180–260 tokens.
- Session pattern: mix of short stateless calls and some longer context sessions (avg session duration ~18s, but heavy sessions up to 120s).
- Latency target: p95 <= 350ms (user-visible interactive flows).
- KV caching: we have a small in-memory session cache; we'd like guidance on prefix caching to reduce cost.

We can upload a sample of 48 hours of anonymized telemetry — here is a placeholder location (we'll grant access once you confirm): s3://opsly-telemetry/2026-04/sample_tokens.tsv

Can you also outline what information you need from us (RPS by hour, prompt/response token histogram, session life distribution, tolerance for quantized model variants, etc.) so we can prioritize?

Thanks,

Sam — really helpful context, thanks. Short answer: we can size a dedicated carveout for that workload, but to get accurate SKU and reserved capacity recommendations we need a short questionnaire + a sample telemetry CSV. I attached a lightweight intake template (opsly_preflight_template.xlsx) — if you can fill the highlighted cells we can turn it into a targeted fleet proposal.

Key fields that speed up sizing (what we most commonly use):
- Peak RPS by 1h window and by 5m window (if you have burst histograms)
- Token histogram: distribution buckets for prompt length and response length (0-50 / 51-150 / 151-300 / 300+)
- Concurrent sessions distribution: how many concurrent sessions per 5m at p50/p95/p99
- Avg and max session KV size (MB) and whether KV is shared across requests or per-session
- Percent of calls that are stateless vs. contextful (we treat stateless as cheap to shard/balance)
- SLOs: p50,p95,p99 latency targets and acceptable tail latency for fallbacks
- Quality tolerance: OK to run a quantized 4/8-bit variant for tail traffic? Willing to accept occasional CPU-fallback?
- Desired reliability SLA and business hours / region constraints

Specific asks I/O: please upload a 48h sample of request timestamps with prompt_token_count and response_token_count columns and an example of a 10-minute burst window. That lets us estimate batching benefit and KV cache hit curve.

Next steps:
1) You fill the opsly_preflight_template.xlsx and drop it in the S3 path you mentioned (we can grab it).
2) Karthik (cc'd) will review and propose an initial SKU mix and a burst pool topology.
3) We schedule a 60m technical sizing workshop (I can run around Wed/Thu next week).

We tend to recommend an exploratory pilot with a small dedicated pool + a burst quota to avoid overcommit up-front; the intake template captures the configuration knobs for that.

Cheers,

Adding a few technical notes that will shape the SKU recommendation:

Short summary of what we'll look for in the telemetry and how we'll translate it to GPUs:
- Effective token throughput determines sustained GPU occupancy. For the prompt/response averages you quoted (~70–100 / 180–260) we typically see batching opportunity for stateless calls; batching reduces per-token kernel overhead but increases latency. We need the burst 5m histogram.
- For mixed short sessions and long context sessions, prefix KV cache push/pull cost matters — please include average KV bytes per session. If KV is small (<100KB) we can keep it in-GPU for many models with moderate GPU memory.
- Multiplexing approach: aim for 60–70% sustained occupancy on primary GPUs and reserve a small hot-burst pool (10–15% of capacity) to absorb the spike. Overcommit is safe with aggressive prefix caching and per-request batching windows tightened to 10–15ms.
- Recommended GPU mix (initial probe): 2 x high-memory GPUs (for long-context/large KV sessions) + 4 x balanced throughput GPUs to handle stateless and batched requests. We'll convert that to specific SKUs in the proposal.
- Fallbacks & variants: keep a quantized 4-bit variant for non-critical tail traffic and a CPU fallback for low-priority background jobs. Please indicate if you cannot tolerate any quantized variants (affects unit cost).
- Autoscaling: for a 3x burst to 90 RPS, an elastic burst pool is more cost-effective than overcommitting reserved nodes; we can propose a reserved baseline + burst credits.

I'll draft a quick one-page sku + topology PDF after we get the telemetry and template filled.

Karthik
